# The `eco` command line

Every command of `eco`, with its arguments and flags, exactly as the binary's
own help prints them. This page is generated: `mise run cli:gen` writes it from
`eco --help` and the help of every subcommand under it, and `mise run check`
fails when it no longer matches the binary. To change a line here, change the
command's definition in `src/main.rs` and run `mise run cli:gen`.

The commands reach eco in three ways.

- `setup` and `bench` run on their own. They need no daemon.
- `start`, `stop`, `restart` and `status` manage the daemon. `start` starts the
  `eco.service` user unit through `systemctl --user` when nothing answers on the
  socket, waits for the socket, and opens the window unless `--headless`. `stop`
  asks the daemon over the socket to stop and waits until it has. They print one
  line of plain text, such as `eco: daemon stopped`; `status` exits 3 when the
  daemon is not running.
- Every other command talks to the running daemon over its socket,
  `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/eco.sock`, and prints one JSON object on one line:
  `{"ok": true, "data": …}`, or `{"ok": false, "code": …, "message": …}` with
  exit code 1. With no daemon the code is `daemon.offline`. `export` is the one
  exception: it prints the WebVTT document itself, to pipe or redirect.

Agents use the same commands through the `eco` skill (`skills/eco/SKILL.md`).
Commands the user service and the daemon run for themselves are hidden from the
help, and so from this page.

---

## `eco`

Voice sessions with an AI beside them, for Omarchy

- **Usage:** `eco <COMMAND>`

```text
Commands:
  setup        Download the models and keep the agent skill current
  start        Start the daemon service and open its window
  stop         Stop the running daemon
  restart      Restart the daemon and reopen its window if it was visible
  status       Show whether the daemon is running
  bench        Measure what docs/benchmarks.md reports
  sessions     List stored sessions, newest first, as JSON
  show         Show a session's summary and timeline
  delete       Permanently delete a paused or ended session
  rename       Give a session a new title and/or kind
  ask          Ask a session a question and wait for the answer
  action       Run a configured action on a session and wait for the answer
  translate    Translate a session's lines and answers below each one, into a language from now on
  send         Run the hook of the action that gave an answer (its id in `eco show`) and wait for it
  note         Keep a note in a session: a fact later answers use, not a question
  export       Print a session's transcript as WebVTT, e.g. `eco export <id> > session.vtt`
  speaker      Say who a speaker of a session is (its label, as `eco show` lists it)
  assign       Assign one line or every speaker in a session to a person
  participant  Link a person to a session, independently of speaker identification
  context      Show or change which context slots a session has on
  line         Change one line of a session, named by who said it and its `at` (see `eco show`)
  tag          The tags that group sessions, several per session
  people       The people linked to sessions; without a subcommand, list them
  import       Import an audio or video file into a new session
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version
```

## `eco bench diarization`

Diarization error rate over recordings with reference RTTMs

- **Usage:** `eco bench diarization [OPTIONS] <DIR>`

```text
Arguments:
  <DIR>  Directory of `<name>.wav` (16 kHz mono) with `<name>.rttm` and optional `<name>.uem`

Options:
      --list <LIST>            File naming the recordings to run, one per line
      --model <MODEL>          Speaker embedding model (ONNX); the one `eco setup` downloads by default
      --threshold <THRESHOLD>  Clustering thresholds to compare, e.g. 0.5,0.6,0.7 [default: 0.65]
      --min-share <MIN_SHARE>  Smallest share of the speech a speaker may hold [default: 0.02]
      --collar <COLLAR>        Seconds forgiven around reference boundaries, half on each side [default: 0]
      --output <OUTPUT>        Directory to write eco's turns to as `<name>.rttm` (first threshold)
  -h, --help                   Print help
```

## `eco tag`

The tags that group sessions, several per session

- **Usage:** `eco tag <COMMAND>`

```text
Commands:
  list    Every tag, with how many sessions carry it
  add     Tag a session; a tag another session has keeps the case it was first written in
  remove  Take a tag off a session
  rename  Rename a tag in every session; renaming it to another tag joins the two
  delete  Take a tag off every session
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

## `eco people`

The people linked to sessions; without a subcommand, list them

- **Usage:** `eco people [COMMAND]`

```text
Commands:
  adopt   Link named live speakers from older sessions to people
  add     Keep a new person by a name no one has yet
  rename  Rename a person in every session that names them
  merge   `from` is the same person as `into`: merge their voices and sessions
  forget  Delete a person and the voices kept for them; sessions keep the name
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

## `eco import`

Import an audio or video file into a new session

- **Usage:** `eco import [OPTIONS] <PATH>`

```text
Arguments:
  <PATH>  

Options:
      --title <TITLE>              
      --kind <KIND>                
      --language <LANGUAGE>        
      --participant <PARTICIPANT>  Who the file is heard as; the user by default
      --date <DATE>                When the recording began, local time: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS]. By default the date the file was recorded with, else when it last changed
      --no-wait                    Return once the import starts instead of when it ends
  -h, --help                       Print help
```
